thread:
alex: Heads-up — since 06:14 UTC we've been seeing p99 latency jumps on prod v2 routes, coincident with the kernel-selector rollout. p95 ~3x baseline, some tenants showing sustained tails.
claire: saw the alert. any rollout ID or git sha?
alex: rollout 2026-03-18T06:00Z, sha a1b2c3f — kernel-selector change introduced a shorter lookahead (hysteresis removed).
jyoti: attaching quick flame summary from the 06:20 window — KV cache churn higher than usual. suspect rapid kernel switches causing context cache resets.
jyoti: ```kernel_choice_counters: fast_kernel=42 slow_kernel=58
selector_transitions: 1234/sec
kv_evictions: +72% vs baseline
batch_size_p50=1 p95=8 p99=64
cpu_ibuf_stalls=18%``` 
marco: this matches a hysteresis regression hypothesis — without hysteresis the selector oscillates on borderline sequences. oscillation causes more kernel loads and thrashes per-tenant KV state.
samir: can we short-circuit to stable kernel for noisy tenants? propose a runtime throttle/fallback policy: if selector transitions > 100/s for a shard, pin to safe_kernel for 10m.
alex: agree. Also want to try toggling the selector hysteresis flag back on while we triage.
claire: I can flip the FF. candidate flag: `runtime.selector_hysteresis`.
marco: also add batching tweak: temporarily prefer larger max_batch_window for affected pods to avoid tiny batches that exacerbate switching.
alex: plan: 1) enable FF rollback (hysteresis=true) 2) enable per-tenant pin fallback for noisy tenants 3) increase max_batch_window from 8ms->20ms on the rollout pool. doing steps in that order.
deploy-bot: @alex deployment request received: toggle `runtime.selector_hysteresis=true` to rollout-pool. Starting rollout to 6 pods.
incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-18-0123 - Runtime selector oscillation causing p99 spikes. Priority: P1. Ops channel: #incidents.
claire: FF toggle done on 6 pods — verifying metrics.
jyoti: pushed a sampling profiler snippet to the thread: `nvprof` traces show kernel load latency spikes during transitions, median kernel load ~1.2ms -> spiking to 10-20ms when eviction path triggers.
jyoti: ```nvprof-summary:
kernel_load_time_ms: median=1.2 p95=11.4 p99=19.6
kv_state_ops/sec: +58%
selector_recompute_ms: median=0.6 p95=5.2
``` 
marco: good. can you also dump kernel selection histogram with the new flag enabled to check reduction in transitions?
jyoti: new counters after FF: selector_transitions: 34/sec (was 1234/sec), kv_evictions - down 60%, p99 trending toward baseline.
samir: I'll stage the per-tenant pin policy. rule: if transitions_per_minute > 500 for tenant -> route to `safe_kernel_v1` for 10m and add tenant to noisy-tenant list for manual review.
alex: go ahead. also please enable a short-term throttle at the shard ingress at 90% of usual QPS for the most impacted shards to prevent domino CPU saturation.
samir: throttle applied to shard-17 and shard-21. observing reduced queue depth.
claire: metrics look much better after FF and throttle: p95 back to ~1.1x baseline, p99 still a hair high but trending down. will keep monitors pinned to 5m.
marco: follow-up: we should add selector hysteresis into the default algorithm and add a unit test for borderline sequence lengths. this regression shouldn't reach prod without a canary that simulates noisy tenants.
alex: agreed. next steps: revert rollout, promote hysteresis permanent, add automated test, add a metric for selector_flapping_rate and alert if >100/s per pool.
jyoti: note for postmortem: also observed batching window antagonism — tiny batches lead to selector churn because input lengths flip heuristics; we'll run a sim with synthetic short sequences.
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-18-0123 updated: mitigations applied (FF, shard throttle, per-tenant pin). Transitioning to monitoring phase.
claire: I'm adding a small dashboard tile showing `selector_transitions` + `kv_evictions` side-by-side for easier triage next time.
alex: thanks everyone. if p99 stabilizes for 30m we can close. once stable, let's schedule a short postmortem with action items: hysteresis as default, flapping alert, batching sim, per-tenant fallback policy to be codified.
marco: I'll own the postmortem writeup. tagging @samir for rollout guard PRs and @jyoti for profiling artifacts.
samir: copy — will prepare PR with safe_kernel routing and throttle knobs.
jyoti: I'll attach the full profiles and flamegraphs to the postmortem.
claire: closing loop: p99 back to baseline at 06:45 UTC. will leave monitors at elevated sensitivity for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
